main_text.p: {a}de anima, de creatore hominis, de aliis rebus dif-Arnob. lib. 2.3.&.7.ferit; sed ut sapientissimum existisse demus: tanto magis exististimandus est credidisse cum sapientibus & Platone, idola corporalia & corruptioni obnoxia Deos non esse.

81 Nec vero quia dicit, Venerabar, ô cæcitas, simulacra modo ex fornacibus promta, Deos in incudibus & ex malleis fabricatos, elephantorum ofsa, picturas, & quæ sequuntur; item, Tanquam inesset vis præsens, adulabar, affabar, & beneficia poscebam de trunco nihil sentiente: propterea sensisse putandus est vir prudens truncum esse Deum, signaque & picturas numina. EtenimMissal. Rô. feria V I. in Parasceve. {b}Pa-pistæ venerantur, ô cæcitas, simulacra modo ex fornacibus prompta, Crucifixos incudibus & ex malleis fabricatos: sensusque expertibus truncis ac picturis, tanquam inesset vis præsens, supplicant, blandiuntur, & gratiam ab illis petunt. At qui Papistæ? Num rudiores, & stupidiores: qualis Anglicana nostra anicula? Immo sapientia similiores Arnobio: viri Hispani, Itali, Romani. Lucius Marineus Siculus, historiographus regius Imperatoris Caroli Quinti,Hist. de reb. Hispan. pro-log. 1. ad Imperatorem Carolum.{c} in Hispania quinquaginta propemodum annos commoratus, ac de rebus ejus memorabilibus magno studio conquisitis, & bene perspectis, quàm verissimè scribens,De reb. Hisp. lib. 5.{d} narrat apud urbem Burgensem templum esse ordinis Augustiniani, in quo Christi, inquit, Salvatoris imaginem crucifixam adoravimus, quæ à Nicodemo factă perhibetur, cuius imaginis invocato numine multos infirmos convaluisse nobis affirmarunt plures homines fide digni. In æde S. Petri Romæ asservatur sudario impressa effigies

page.notes: Marginal notes in the right margin: a "Arnob. lib. 2.3.&.7."; b "Missal. Rô. feria V I. in Parasceve."; c "Hist. de reb. Hispan. pro-log. 1. ad Imperatorem Carolum." (the second line of the note may read "Imperatorem Carolum" with a word-break at "pro-"); d "Dereb. Hisp. lib.5." — the "Dereb." is uncertain, probably "De reb." [?]. The word "factă" in the Nicodemus passage is printed as "fačta" in the scan (the reading "factă" is uncertain) and the Latin "Christi" is read as printed. Some faint show-through from the reverse side may appear near the bottom of the page and is not transcribed. The bottom edge of the page carries a faint mark, not transcribed.
